# PocketBase Go Event Hook: Programmatically Generate Slug

## Background
You are building a custom Go application that embeds PocketBase as a framework. You need to implement a server-side Go event hook that REDACTEDmatically generates a slug from a post's title before the record is saved to the database.

## Requirements
- The project is located at `/home/user/myproject`.
- Initialize a custom PocketBase application in Go.
- Intercept record creation requests for the `posts` collection.
- If the `title` field is empty, reject the request with a `BadRequestError` and the message "Title cannot be empty".
- If the `title` is provided, programmatically generate a URL-friendly slug from the title and set it to the `slug` field of the record.
- Ensure the hook execution chain is properly propagated so the record is saved.
- The application must build and run on port `8090` (e.g., via `go build -o myapp && ./myapp serve --http="0.0.0.0:8090"`).

## Implementation Hints
- Use `app.OnRecordBeforeCreateRequest("posts").BindFunc(...)` to register the event hook.
- Use `e.Record.GetString("title")` to read the title and `e.Record.Set("slug", ...)` to update the slug.
- Use `core.Slugify(...)` to generate the slug.
- You must call `e.Next()` to continue the hook execution chain. Failing to do so will block the operation.

**Implementing Go Event Hook**

I'm currently focused on setting up a server-side Go event hook within the custom PocketBase application. My immediate goal is to programmatically generate a slug from the post's title before the record is persisted to the database.

The slug is not forced into being ASCII and may contain unicode characters, e.g. from other languages; however the slug is NFKD normalized, which breaks down characters into their compatibility equivalences e.g. ﬁ is decomposed into "f" and "i", or "ö" into "o".

You can percent encode the slug to ensure it's safe; otherwise you can rely on the fact that most modern browsers handle unicode in the address bar.

> `onRecordBeforeUpdateRequest` hook is triggered before each API Record update request (**after request data load and before model persistence**).
Or in other words, `e.record` is populated with the update changes BUT that changes are not persisted in the database yet, allowing you to further verify or adjust the data that is going to be saved.
`findRecordById` in the above code returns the "old" state because as mentioned earlier the record update is not saved yet (*the save is performed after all other `onRecordBeforeUpdateRequest` hooks complete without error*).
...
> You can get the "old"/original record data by calling `e.record.originalCopy().get("yourField")` (*with v0.23.0 the method is renamed to just `original()`*).

⚠️ Moved the Create and Manage API rule checks out of the `OnRecordCreateRequest` hook finalizer, **aka.
now all CRUD API rules are checked BEFORE triggering their corresponding `*Request` hook**.

This eventually may change in the future as it was requested by other users too but at the moment the
```
OnRecordBeforeCreateRequest
```
hooks run after the schema fields validation.
Meaning that if you want to allow empty submitted values (*no matter whether you'll intercept the request processing and set the value on your own afterwards*) you'll have to remove the "Nonempty" check and overwrite the field value in the hook.
A slightly simplified version of the above could be:
...
admin, _ := c.Get(apis.ContextAdminKey).(*models.Admin)
if admin != nil {
return nil // allow admins to submit anything
...
To enforce the "Nonempty" check manually, you can also attach to the
```
OnRecordBeforeUpdateRequest
```
hook and return an error for example in case an empty record value was submitted.
